facts.tasselled-wobbegong: The tasselled wobbegong has a fringe of branching skin lobes around its head, and one was photographed on the Great Barrier Reef with a whole bamboo shark head-first in its jaws.
facts.spotted-wobbegong: The spotted wobbegong lies camouflaged on Australian reefs, usually under 2 metres long though reported up to about 3, and has bitten people who stepped on or disturbed it.
facts.heavisides-dolphin: Heaviside's dolphin, found only off Namibia and South Africa, is named after the wrong man: its specimen came from a Captain Haviside, but was credited to a surgeon called Heaviside.
facts.clymene-dolphin: The Clymene dolphin of the Atlantic is the only confirmed case of a marine mammal species that arose as a hybrid, from spinner and striped dolphins.
facts.dalls-porpoise: Dall's porpoise is one of the fastest small cetaceans, throwing up a rooster tail of spray, and Japan's hunt of it was for decades the largest direct hunt of any cetacean.
facts.dubois-sea-snake: Dubois' sea snake of northern Australia has one of the most toxic venoms of any snake, yet it bites only when provoked and hunts fish and moray eels on the seabed.
facts.thick-billed-murre: Thick-billed murres of Arctic and sub-Arctic seas are among the deepest-diving flying birds, with dives recorded to 150 metres and beyond.
facts.coconut-crab: The coconut crab is the largest land-living arthropod, climbs trees and cracks coconuts with claws whose pinch, estimated at up to about 3,300 newtons, is stronger than most animals' bites.
facts.california-halibut: The California halibut is a left-eyed flounder, yet nearly half of all individuals turn out right-eyed, a quirk almost unique among flatfish.
facts.humpback-anglerfish: The humpback anglerfish is the classic toothy black seadevil of the deep; females reach about 15 centimetres while the males are only around 2 centimetres long.
facts.veined-squid: The veined squid is one of the main squid caught around Britain and Ireland, and can hover in place and change colour in an instant.
facts.vent-barnacle: Vent barnacles grow in dense clusters on vent chimneys, with long bristly feeding legs coated in filamentous bacteria that are thought to be part of their diet.
facts.ethereal-snailfish: The ethereal snailfish was filmed at 8,145 metres in the Mariana Trench in 2014, a wispy, nearly transparent fish known only from video, as none has yet been caught.
facts.apo-reef: Apo Reef off Mindoro in the Philippines is the largest atoll-like reef in the country and is often described as the second-largest contiguous coral reef in the world.
facts.blue-starfish: The blue starfish of Indo-Pacific reefs is a vivid blue and can regrow lost arms; its close relative Linckia multifora can even grow a whole new star from a single severed arm.
facts.gulf-of-st-lawrence: The Gulf of St Lawrence, where the St Lawrence River meets the Atlantic, is one of the largest estuarine systems in the world, and ice covers the whole gulf in January and February.
facts.guanabara-bay: Guanabara Bay is the great bay on which Rio de Janeiro stands, named River of January by Portuguese sailors who reached it in January 1502 and, by tradition, took it for a river mouth.
facts.uss-albatross: The Albatross, launched in 1882, is often called the first ship built specifically for marine research, and it dredged up thousands of new species.
facts.molasses-reef: Molasses Reef off Key Largo, Florida, lies inside the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary and is one of the most popular dive and snorkel sites in the Keys.
facts.arapaima: The arapaima of the Amazon must surface regularly to gulp air and has been verified at just over 3 metres long.
facts.slate-pencil-urchin: The slate pencil urchin's thick, blunt reddish spines look like old-fashioned slate pencils and have been used to make wind chimes and jewellery.
facts.vigo: Vigo, in Galicia, is one of the biggest fishing ports in the world, landing fish from fleets that work the Atlantic as far away as the Falklands.
facts.bombay-duck: Bombay duck is not a duck but a lizardfish caught in huge numbers off western India, where it is dried in the open air and fried.
facts.yellowtail-amberjack: The yellowtail amberjack is a prized game fish off California, Baja and Australia and is served as hiramasa in sushi bars, distinct from the Japanese yellowtail sold as hamachi.
facts.pollock: Pollock, a cod relative, produce thumping sounds with their swim bladder when handled or cornered, a trait shared with cod and haddock, which grunt during spawning.
facts.tiger-tail-seahorse: The tiger tail seahorse of South-East Asia is named for the dark bands on its tail and, with the common seahorse, makes up most of the Philippine seahorse catch.
facts.picasso-triggerfish: The Picasso triggerfish wears a pattern of blue, black and yellow stripes that looks painted on, and it drums by beating its pectoral fins against its swim bladder.
facts.coral-trout: The coral trout is a red, blue-spotted grouper of the Great Barrier Reef, not a trout at all, and one of the most valuable fish in Queensland's reef fishery.
facts.gentoo-penguin: The gentoo is the fastest-swimming penguin, reaching about 36 kilometres per hour, and feeds on krill and fish close to shore.
facts.kronosaurus: Kronosaurus was a Cretaceous pliosaur from Queensland, Australia, whose skull alone is estimated at over 2 metres long.
facts.triops: Triops tadpole shrimp hatch in temporary pools from eggs that can wait years in dry dust, and tadpole shrimp that look much like them were already around more than 200 million years ago.
facts.slit-shell-snail: Slit shell snails of deep tropical slopes belong to a family with a fossil record back to the Cambrian, around 500 million years ago, and their shells are prized by collectors.
facts.bougainville-trench: The Bougainville Trench curves through the northern Solomon Sea west of Bougainville Island, continuing the New Britain Trench, whose Planet Deep exceeds 9,000 metres.
facts.bristle-worm: Bristle worms are segmented worms with paddle-like feet fringed with bristles, and they have been collected from trench floors more than 10,000 metres down.
facts.japanese-sea-lion: The Japanese sea lion bred on beaches of Japan and Korea until hunting wiped it out; the last reliable sightings were in the 1950s, with a final juvenile reported in 1974.
facts.smooth-handfish: The smooth handfish of Tasmania, known from one specimen collected in 1802, was declared extinct in 2020, the first modern marine fish so listed, though the IUCN later reset it to data deficient.
facts.dragon-hole: The Dragon Hole in the South China Sea plunges roughly 300 metres into the reef and was the deepest known blue hole until the Taam Ja' Blue Hole off Mexico was measured deeper in 2024.
facts.mediterranean-damselfish: The Mediterranean damselfish is the only native damselfish in the Mediterranean, a dark fish whose juveniles are brilliant blue, common in shoals above rocks.
facts.mediterranean-parrotfish: The Mediterranean parrotfish is the only native parrotfish in the Mediterranean, prized by the Romans, and is spreading north as the sea warms.
facts.giant-warty-squid: The giant warty squid of Antarctic waters can reach more than 2 metres in total length and is a food of sperm whales and other Southern Ocean predators.
